chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abdullah ibn Ibrahim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

‘What are your physicians instructing you with regarding the Citron?’ So I said, ‘They are instructing us that we eat it before the meal’. So he (peace be upon him) said: ‘I am ordering you all with it after the meal’.

key_terms.الْأُتْرُجِّ: the citron (a type of citrus fruit)

ai.seo_question: When should one eat citron according to the Imam's instruction?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the nuanced relationship between empirical medical knowledge and the Imam’s authoritative guidance, where the physician’s recommendation to eat citron before meals is contrasted with the Imam’s instruction to consume it after. This distinction highlights the concept of *khass* (specific) versus *‘amm* (general) in practical jurisprudence, suggesting that the Imam’s directive may address specific health benefits or spiritual etiquettes not covered by general medical consensus. It underscores the Shia scholarly tradition of valuing both rational inquiry and divine wisdom in daily practices.
